description:
What to do if a shark comes close? The International Shark Attack File confirmed 65 unprovoked shark bites on people worldwide in 2025, counted 29 provoked bites separately, and recorded 12 confirmed shark-related fatalities, nine of them from unprovoked bites. It says the chances of being bitten remain extremely low. If a shark comes close, it says keep eye contact, slowly move away, and leave the water if you can. If it bites, hit the eyes and gills, and do not act passively. A snout hit, ideally with an object, usually only stops the shark for a time. It also advises swim with a buddy, don't swim at dawn or dusk, and stay close to shore.

#sharks #sharkattack #meatballmyths #shorts

Source: International Shark Attack File, Florida Museum of Natural History (2025 yearly summary; Quick Tips; How to Avoid a Shark Attack; Advice to Swimmers; Sharks vs. Lightning Fatalities). General information, not safety training.
